description: Questions for Demo 3 (The Hound of the Baskervilles). Every answer was checked against data/hound/passages.json; 'evidence' lists the passage ids that state it. Rubrics are LLM-free: every all_of group needs at least one phrase present (case-insensitive substring).

questions.question: In The Hound of the Baskervilles, who gave Dr. Mortimer the walking stick he left at Baker Street, according to its engraving?
questions.answer: His friends of the C.C.H. - Charing Cross Hospital ("To James Mortimer, M.R.C.S., from his friends of the C.C.H.").

questions.question: What did Dr. Mortimer see on the ground near Sir Charles Baskerville's body that he did not mention at the inquest?
questions.answer: The footprints of a gigantic hound.

questions.question: How was the anonymous warning note that Sir Henry received at his London hotel made?
questions.answer: From words cut out of a Times leading article and pasted onto the paper; only the word 'moor' was written in ink.

questions.question: Who is the escaped convict hiding on the moor, and how is he connected to the Barrymores?
questions.answer: Selden, the Notting Hill murderer; he is Mrs. Barrymore's younger brother.

questions.question: What is the true relationship between Stapleton and the woman who lives with him as his sister?
questions.answer: She is his wife, posing as his sister.

questions.question: What had been put on the hound to make it glow in the dark?
Who wrote the letter signed 'L. L.' that brought Sir Charles to the gate on the night he died, and who had persuaded her to write it?
questions.answer: Laura Lyons of Coombe Tracey wrote it (chapters 10-11); Stapleton had persuaded her, having promised to marry her (chapter 13).

questions.question: Who is Stapleton really, and why did he want Sir Henry dead?
questions.answer: He is a Baskerville - the son of Rodger Baskerville, Sir Charles's younger brother - and wanted to inherit the Baskerville estate and title (portrait in chapter 13, Holmes's explanation in chapter 15).
